title: Full list: NDC unveils 2027 presidential campaign council
summary: NDC says its 2027 campaign council will coordinate nationwide campaigning and mobilise support for its vision for Nigeria. The announcement gave no membership details.
body:
The NDC has announced a presidential campaign council for the 2027 election. The party said the body would coordinate its campaign across the country and mobilise support for its vision of a new, just and prosperous Nigeria.

The information available about the announcement does not identify council members or describe its structure, responsibilities beyond campaign coordination, or plans for carrying out its work.

The council’s stated role places it at the centre of the party’s preparations for a nationwide presidential campaign. Its task, as outlined by the party, is to organise campaigning and build support around its vision; further details about its membership and activities were not provided.

title: Ebola: NCDC expands health declaration requirement for international travellers
summary: Nigeria’s NCDC is expanding health declaration requirements for international travellers amid Ebola concerns. Implementation guidance is still expected.
body:
Nigeria’s National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) is expanding the health declaration requirement for international travellers in connection with Ebola, according to the report. The agency has sent advisories to the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) and the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA).

Further instructions are expected to guide how the requirement will be implemented in collaboration with airlines. The available information does not specify which travellers or routes are covered, when the expanded requirement will take effect, or what information passengers will be asked to provide.

title: Ebola: Lagos Intensifies Surveillance, Reassures Residents Of Preparedness
summary: Lagos reports no suspected Ebola cases. It is strengthening surveillance after Nigeria confirmed its first Bundibugyo virus case.
body:
The Lagos State Government says there are currently no suspected Ebola cases in the state and that it is strengthening surveillance and response preparations. The measures follow confirmation of Nigeria’s first case of the Bundibugyo virus in the Federal Capital Territory. The state urged residents and visitors to remain calm and rely on official information.

Through the Ministry of Health’s Directorate of Epidemiology, Biosecurity and Global Health, Lagos is increasing disease monitoring, public communication and community engagement. It is also working with agencies at points of entry, including Murtala Muhammed International Airport. A recent engagement at the airport involved its management, Port Health Services and other aviation and public health stakeholders, with discussions covering passenger screening, information sharing, infection prevention and emergency coordination.

The state is distributing information about Ebola symptoms, transmission and prevention. It says the disease is mainly spread through direct contact with the blood or other body fluids of a symptomatic infected person, contaminated materials or the bodies of people who have died from the disease. Contact with infected animals can also result in infection. Symptoms may appear between two and 21 days after exposure and include fever, weakness, headache, muscle pain, sore throat, vomiting, diarrhoea and abdominal pain; unexplained bleeding or bruising may occur in some cases.

Because early symptoms can resemble malaria and other common illnesses, the government advises people who feel unwell, particularly after possible exposure or travel from an area with active transmission, to seek prompt medical assessment. Under Lagos’s fever-management policy, a person with fever should have a malaria rapid diagnostic test before taking antimalarial medicines. Anyone concerned about possible Ebola exposure is urged to contact public health authorities before going to a healthcare facility. In Lagos, concerns can be reported through emergency numbers 112 or 767, or to the state health ministry’s directorate at 0802 316 9485. The state says it will continue monitoring developments and coordinating its preparedness efforts.

title: Police Probe Fatal Shooting Of Two Officers In Kogi
summary: Kogi police are investigating the deaths of two officers in a shooting at ASCO Camp, Ajaokuta. The case has been referred to the state criminal investigations department.
body:
The Kogi State Police Command has opened an investigation into a fatal shooting at ASCO Camp in Ajaokuta that left two serving officers dead. Police said the incident was reported at 11:04 p.m. and that the Divisional Police Officer for Ajaokuta led officers to the scene.

According to the command’s preliminary findings, Corporal Amos Yusuf, who was on night duty, shot his colleague, Corporal Grace Onimisi, and then shot himself. Both officers were taken to separate medical facilities, where they were pronounced dead. Their remains were placed in the mortuary at ASCO Hospital. Police said an AK-47 rifle and four spent cartridges were recovered at the scene.

The case has been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department for further inquiries. Police said the circumstances and motive remain under investigation and that the command would not speculate about details that have not been established. The commissioner of police expressed condolences to the officers’ families, colleagues and loved ones; the command said it would issue verified updates as appropriate.

title: Wike’s scholarship beneficiary emerges ABUAD’s best Law graduate
summary: Scholarship recipient Nengi Donald Jaja has become ABUAD’s top law graduate, earning 12 awards. He says a 2017 Rivers State grant helped make it possible.
body:
Nengi Donald Jaja, who received a Rivers State Government scholarship in 2017, has been named the overall Best Graduating Student in Afe Babalola University’s College of Law. He says he also received 12 awards and was the college’s salutatorian, describing the result as the fulfilment of a goal he had set for himself as a child.

In a post on X, Jaja said the scholarship followed a performance at an event in December 2017. It was intended to fund his education through secondary school and university. A report published by Tribune that month said former Rivers State Governor Nyesom Wike awarded him a ₦40 million scholarship after he sang at a thanksgiving service in Port Harcourt.

Jaja said the support encouraged him to pursue academic achievement while retaining his ambition to become an R&B and soul artiste. He reported earning a 5.00 GPA in eight of his ten university semesters, with scores of 4.96 and 4.87 in the other two. Across his studies, he said, he received 69 As and two Bs, while also holding several leadership positions. He added that he had been the best Arts student in secondary school.

Jaja credited his family, friends and lecturers for supporting him, and said music by singer Tems helped him stay emotionally grounded. He also described himself as the first male student to achieve the College of Law distinction. His account highlights the role the state-funded award played in enabling his education, while his academic record and honours mark the outcome of his studies at ABUAD.

title: Gov Otti offers orphaned debate champion varsity scholarship
summary: Governor Otti has offered a university scholarship to an orphaned debate champion. He also awarded ₦1 million to essay competition winner Onyinyechi Okonkwo.
body:
Governor Otti has offered a university scholarship to an orphaned debate champion, according to the report. The source material does not identify the student or provide details about the scholarship.

Otti also awarded ₦1 million to Onyinyechi Okonkwo of Ovom Girls Secondary School, who won a recent national essay competition.

The report provides no further information about the debate competition or the terms of the scholarship.

title: Death toll in Taraba terror attack rises to 40
summary: The reported death toll from a terror attack in Taraba has risen to 40. Police had earlier confirmed 10 local deaths.
body:
The reported death toll from a terror attack in Taraba has risen to 40, according to Premium Times. The publication had earlier reported that state police confirmed 10 local people were killed.

The latest figure is four times the number initially confirmed by police. The source material does not provide further details about when the attack occurred, where in Taraba it took place or how the higher toll was established.

The increase marks a significant change in the reported scale of the attack. The available information does not identify those responsible or give details about any official response.

title: Real Madrid’s Courtois Out Of Clasico With Flu
summary: Real Madrid ruled Thibaut Courtois out of Sunday’s Clasico against Barcelona after he came down with flu. Andriy Lunin is expected to start.
body:
Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois will miss Sunday’s Clasico against Barcelona after falling ill with flu, the club announced a few hours before the match. Madrid described him as a last-minute withdrawal from the squad.

Ukrainian goalkeeper Andriy Lunin is set to replace Courtois against Barcelona, who are unbeaten under coach Hansi Flick. The match is at Camp Nou.

The absence adds to Madrid’s personnel problems for the game: winger Vinicius Junior is also unavailable because of suspension. Madrid are third in the league, six points behind leaders Barcelona, making the meeting significant to the title race.

title: Police arrest two robbery suspects in Bauchi
summary: Police in Bauchi arrested two people suspected of belonging to a robbery gang. They are accused of robbing residents and injuring them with machetes.
body:
The Bauchi State Police Command has arrested two people suspected of belonging to a gang accused of robbing residents and inflicting machete injuries on them.

The allegations involve both robbery and physical harm to residents. The available information does not say how many people were affected or describe the injuries beyond noting machete wounds.

The arrests were announced by the Bauchi State Police Command. No further details about the suspects, the alleged incidents or the investigation were provided in the supplied report.

title: Heat wave: Anambra first lady urges residents to take precautions
summary: Nonye Soludo urged Anambra residents to stay hydrated as the heat wave intensifies. The advice aims to help prevent heat-related illnesses.
body:
Anambra First Lady Nonye Soludo has urged residents to take precautions as the heat wave intensifies. She cited staying hydrated as one way to help prevent heat-related illnesses.

The appeal highlights the risk of illness during the heat wave and encourages residents to take steps to reduce that risk. The supplied report does not describe specific illnesses or their symptoms.

Hydration is the only precaution named in the report. It does not provide further recommendations or details about the heat wave.

title: EPL: Carrick to bench Brruno for Bournemouth clash — Report
summary: Michael Carrick is reportedly set to leave Bruno Fernandes out of Manchester United’s starting line-up. The match is against Bournemouth.
body:
Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick will reportedly leave club captain Bruno Fernandes out of the starting line-up for the team’s Premier League match against Bournemouth. The report concerns the starting line-up, not whether Fernandes will be involved in the match at all.

The reported decision would mean the club captain is not among United’s starters for the Bournemouth clash. The supplied information does not give a reason for the reported change or say who would take Fernandes’s place.

The report identifies Carrick as Manchester United’s head coach and Fernandes as the club captain. It does not provide further details about the team selection or the match.

title: 2027: Turnout at Kaduna rally shows North’s support for Tinubu — Group
summary: A northern group says turnout at a Kaduna rally signals confidence in Tinubu. It links that support to 2027.
body:
A northern group said the large turnout at a rally in Kaduna showed the region’s confidence in President Bola Tinubu’s leadership ahead of 2027.

The group presented attendance at the rally as evidence of support for Tinubu. The statement links that support to the period ahead of 2027.

The claim is the group’s assessment of the rally turnout. The supplied information does not provide further details about the rally or the group.
